name: usage-lens
description: See where your Kiro credits actually go. Usage Lens reads the gateway's own per-turn usage shards and breaks the spend down by model, surface, agent, scheduled job, and session — hour by hour or day by day — so a repricing, a runaway cron, or a context-bloated session shows up as a shape on a chart instead of a surprise at the end of the month.
author: Kiro Crew community
highlights: Credits broken down by model, surface, agent, cron job, or session — switch dimension without reloading
Hourly or daily granularity over 1, 3, 7, 14, or 30 days, with every figure compared against the preceding window of equal length
Per-job rollup for scheduled work: a cron that starts a fresh session per run is still one row, not hundreds
Unit-cost trend (credits per turn) separates a price change from doing more work
Automatic flag when a model's credits-per-turn jumps by half or more against the prior window
Reads only the local usage shards the gateway already writes — no account linking, no network calls, no writes
useCases: Find out which scheduled job is quietly eating your monthly credits, and how much a change to its interval would save.
Tell a model repricing apart from doing more work, by reading credits per turn instead of credits per day.
Reconcile against Kiro's own meter for the current billing cycle and see how much of your spend never went through the gateway.
configuration: No account linking and no configuration: the app reads the usage shards the gateway already writes under usage/tokens, and the billing comparison reuses the figures the gateway has already fetched.
Enabling it requires trusting its Python (agent.apps_trusted), because the backend runs inside the gateway process. It declares no storage, cron, spawn, or network permission.
